WHAT TO DO IN CASE
AN EMERGENCY WATER
LANDING IS NECESSARY
HOW TO LAUNCH AND INFLATE RAFTS
CEILING RAFT COMPARTMENTS
1. To open ceiling raft compart-
ment, pull this handle down.
2. Release buckles and lift raft off
door. Launch out nearest exit.
YOUR LIFE VEST
Individual life vest is in a
pouch under seat. Pull Tab
to open for access to vest.
1. NO SMOKING. Adjust your seat back to upright
position.
2. Remove high heeled shoes, shoes with metal cleats
and all cumbersome, restrictive clotning.
Loosen your
collar and tie. Remove things that obviously could hurt
you, suen as glasses and taise teen, sharp objects such
as pens, pencils and brooches.
3. Put on your life vest. It is stowed under your seat.
Do not inflate Life Vest inside Airplane.
4. Sit down and fasten your seat belt. Pull it up good
and tight; this is important. Locate the emergency exits
nearest you.
5. Before landing, your Captain will issue a "Brace for
Ditching" order.
Assume brace position as shown on
back of this card. This position will reduce the shock of
sudden deceleration.
6. After all forward motion has stopped, not before,
unfasten your seatbelt and proceed immediately to
nearest exit. Your crew will direct you to rafts.

The 4 Astroliner
AmericanAirlines
FOR YOUR SAFETY - Know how to move out of
this airplane fast. There is fire-danger any time a landing
is other than normal-particularly when the airplane structure
is damaged. On the back of this card is a floor plan of the
plane you are in. Familiarize yourself with the location of
the exits. Note particularly the exits nearest you. Study
the brace position you should assume during an emergency
landing and also how the doors are opened as shown in the
figures below. When leaving, move immediately to the exits.
Do not go back for coats, purses or other personal items.
YOUR SEAT BELT - It is recommended that seat belts be kept fastened at all times - even when the seat
belt sign is off.
1 Rotate door handle 180 degrees.
Door initially moves inward slight-
ly and then is automatically pow-
ered outward to a fully open posi-
tion.

and begins inflating

doorway. Do not try to slow yourself down; special
pads at the bottom will reduce your speed. Move
away from the bottom of the slide quickly.

OXYGEN MASK
TEN EMERGENCY EXIT ROUTES
Should a change in cabin pressure occur while at high
altitude, a door above you will open and an oxygen
mask will automatically drop within your reach.
STOP ALL SMOKING. Take the nearest mask and
pull toward you, this starts flow of oxygen.
Place
mask over nose and mouth
and breathe normally.

UPPER DECK EMERGENCY EXIT ROUTES
In the event of an emergency evacuation, descend
the spiral staircase to the main deck and then move
swiftly to one of the door exits.
If you are unable to do so, the crew service door is
also an emergency exit. It is located forward and to
the right of the upper deck lavatory. A crew member
will open the door and inflate the slide if it should be
required.
